name: 白腰雨燕

similarSpecies.distinction: Substantive identification/range/conservation read. 16–18cm sexes similar. Large all-dark swift scythe-shaped narrow wings deeply forked tail, dark brown subtly scaled body/mantle, paler forehead/throat, dark rump vs white rump Pacific; smaller slimmer narrower wing than Pacific. Inner flight feathers paler than coverts in good light. apus breeds Europe/NW Africa to Baikal/Iran, winters Africa; pekinensis Iran/west Himalaya/Mongolia/N China, winters E/S Africa with small numbers N India/Arabia. LC stable. HK accidental/very rare migrant, multiple midwinter records.

Runtime House Swift taxonomy retained. More compact swift with contrasting WHITE RUMP, pale chin/throat and shallow tail fork, unlike grey-brown Himalayan rump. Current external sources lump nipalensis group into Apus affinis; no runtime taxonomic migration authorized.

rangeMap.note: 17–20cm sexes alike. Long scythe wings and long relatively deeply forked tail, all blackish brown apart contrasting WHITE RUMP band and indistinct pale throat, pale fringed underparts; substantially larger than House Swift. Nominate breeds Siberia/Kamchatka/NChina/Japan, winters Indonesia/Melanesia/Australia. kurodae (kanoi synonym treatment differs) EChina to Guangdong/SJapan/Taiwan/NPhilippines, winters Malaysia/Indonesia/Philippines. Western Guangdong/E Guangxi boundary obscured by Cook swift; map not occurrence polygon. LC stable globally despite local HK migrant decline, local offshore island breeding. Full-world partial native-country overview, not whole-country occupancy, precise seasons or complete range.
